speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Minister for Transport in view of the rising petrol prices, whether the Ministry has considered giving support to the point-to-point (P2P) sector to help defray such costs as the industry faces a slow start to passenger recovery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Government actively monitors the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the point-to-point (P2P) sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: At Budget 2021, the Government raised the petrol duty as part of Singapore’s sustainability drive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This has bolstered the incomes of our P2P drivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We will continue to monitor the P2P sector and the demand for such services to ensure that drivers are coping well in this challenging period.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Our P2P drivers have given feedback on the rising costs to their businesses, such as the impending GST hikes, in addition to what we had mentioned about the rising petrol cost.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: When was the last time meter and flag-down rates were revised, and would the Ministry and the Public Transport Council be looking at revising flag-down fares or fare structures for both the taxi and private hire services?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, taxi and Private Hire Car (PHC) operators have actually been making adjustments to their fares over the years.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, most recently, a PHC operator actually adjusted the fares last year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The operators are responsible for adjusting the taxi and PHC fares, taking into account prevailing market conditions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And I think they are best placed to do so, to better match the supply and demand of P2P services even as they take into account their own cost structures as well as, of course, ensuring that fares remain competitive, given the landscape.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This will also allow market forces to effectively respond in a timely manner and also encourage the service providers to improve their service offerings.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, there have been benefits to this approach.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: You can see that there is high vehicle availability during peak hours.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We also want to ensure that these fares are transparent, easy to understand, so that commuters can make an informed choice.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to fuel cost, for instance, one of the ways really would be for them to do more ride hails and reduce the mileage clocked from plying the streets.
